summary: Wave 3 (Ecosystem Live) validation. Executed 5 pytest suites (realtime, integrations, media, email, foryou) with -n 1: 36/36 passed in ~74s. Frontend homepage verified via Playwright: feed-tabs + feed-tab-latest + feed-tab-for-you present, all 5 live widgets rendered (crypto, fx, weather, rss, youtube) with correct status badges (2 ACTIVE + 2 CONFIG_PENDING visible; crypto flapping to ERROR). Backend public endpoints sanity-checked directly against REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL: /api/widgets/all returns dict with 5 providers, /api/email/status=CONFIG_PENDING with from_name, /api/feed/for-you degrades to CHRONOLOGICAL without auth, /api/realtime/stream returns 401 without cookie (correct). MessagesPage/notifications-bell UI is gated behind Emergent Google Auth (route is /mensajes) so cannot be exercised end-to-end without a real Google session, but source confirms data-testid=messages-realtime-status exists on line 70 of MessagesPage.jsx.

minor.issue: Intermittent status=ERROR from CoinGecko upstream 429 rate limit. Fallback data (last known bitcoin/ethereum prices) is still returned, so UI does not break, but review request expected status=ACTIVE. Recommend adding server-side cache TTL / stale-while-revalidate so repeated public traffic doesn't hit CoinGecko every request.

action_items: Consider adding server-side cache (30-60s TTL) around CoinGecko fetch in services/integrations/crypto.py so intermittent 429s don't flip status to ERROR when data is still valid.
Optional: expose /mensajes route also as /messages alias for symmetry (minor UX).
critical_code_review_comments: Wave 3 file layout is clean: realtime broker isolated, provider integrations follow a shared WidgetResponse envelope with graceful degradation, feed engine composed of small provider classes. Good separation of concerns.

Crypto integration lacks a short-lived success cache; each public request hits CoinGecko free tier which will 429 under mild traffic. Suggest in-memory TTL cache or Mongo-backed last_success snapshot serving ACTIVE for N seconds after any success.
Email routes correctly returning CONFIG_PENDING with ok=true dry-run behavior when EMERGENT_EMAIL_KEY is absent — good pattern.
seed_data_creation: None new — pytest suites manage their own transient fixtures.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All wave3 suites pass with -n 1 (xdist scheduling still flaky pre-Wave3, unrelated). Frontend messages/notifications-bell tests require an actual Emergent Google session; source confirms the testids exist. If CoinGecko flips to ERROR again in future runs, it's the same upstream 429 issue — data payload still populated via fallback.
